title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 673-675 of the 'Longue Marche' continuation). Grothendieck works over a base S_0, probably Spec Z, with ring schemes. Starting from a ring A, an ideal J = N·A and quotient B = A/J, he builds a ring scheme A_[N]. It sits in an extension (71) of the constant ring scheme B_{S_0} by a 'scheme version' of J, which is apparently J ≅ G_a via λ ↦ Nλ. Taking multiplicative groups gives (72): 1 → (1+J)^* → A_[N]^* → (B^*)_{S_0} → 1. Here (1+J)^* is described in (73) as pairs (λ,λ') with λ+λ'+λλ'=0, i.e. 1+λ is invertible.

Specialisation A = Z, J = NZ gives (74): 1 → (1+NZ)^* → O_N^* → (Z/NZ)^*_{S_0} → 1.

This page:
- (75) defines (1+NZ)^* = {λ in the additive ring scheme 'Z̃ = Z̃_0' (essentially G_a over S_0) | 1+Nλ invertible}. In modern terms this is the affine group scheme Spec Z[λ, 1/(1+Nλ)]. Its group law, transported from (1+Nλ)(1+Nλ') = 1+N(λ+λ'+Nλλ'), is λ*λ' = λ+λ'+Nλλ'. This is G_m over Z[1/N] and degenerates to G_a in characteristic p | N.
- He notes that the O_N form a projective system of ring schemes (in N, ordered by divisibility), and the O_N^* a projective system of commutative group schemes. He explicitly declines to study the structure of these systems or their projective limits, a question that arises for general A.
- Instead he makes explicit the kernels (76) of O_N^* → O_1^* = O^* (the units of the N = 1 object).
- (77) The kernel consists of the 1+N[λ] with 1+Nλ = 1, i.e. Nλ = 0. As a bare scheme it is the N-torsion _N Z̃_0 of the additive scheme, Spec Z[λ]/(Nλ).

The next page notes that this kernel is trivial over Z[1/N] and has nontrivial fibres at p | N. It then specialises to N = 12, where (Z/12)^* ≅ μ_2 × μ_2, with characters ε_2, ε_3 and their additive versions ν_2, ν_3. This is presumably aimed at the order-12 phenomena of SL_2(Z) / the Teichmüller tower studied in the Longue Marche.
errors: On (77): since Nλ = 0 on this kernel, the induced law λ+λ'+Nλλ' is just addition. So the kernel is _N G_a, Spec Z[λ]/(Nλ), with its additive law. Its fibres at p | N are then G_a, not G_m as the neighbouring transcription reads. Either the transcription is wrong or Grothendieck means the fibres of (1+NZ)^* in a different sense. Over Z[1/N] it is G_m that appears, for the full (1+NZ)^*.
Spec Z[λ]/(Nλ) is not flat over Z for N ≠ 1, because it has N-torsion. The next-page phrase '... plat si N≠1' should most likely read 'non plat'.
The exact definition of the ring scheme A_[N] (how λ ↦ Nλ glues to the constant part) is not fully specified on these pages. The reconstruction is therefore partly conjectural.

ideas.what: Group scheme (1+NZ)^* = Spec Z[λ,1/(1+Nλ)] with law λ+λ'+Nλλ', interpolating between G_m (N invertible) and G_a (N = 0)
ideas.modern_name: Deformation group scheme G^{(λ)} (Waterhouse–Weisfeiler; Sekiguchi–Oort–Suwa), 'from Artin–Schreier to Kummer'

ideas.what: Ring scheme A_[N], an extension of the constant ring Z/N by a scheme-theoretic ideal 'NZ'; its unit group extends (Z/N)^* by (1+NZ)^*
ideas.modern_name: Ring scheme thickening / congruence-unit group scheme; loosely related to Witt-type ring schemes

ideas.what: Projective system in N of the ring schemes O_N and unit group schemes O_N^*; limits deliberately not studied
ideas.modern_name: Pro-ring-scheme analogue of Ẑ = lim Z/N

ideas.what: Kernel of O_N^* → O_1^* is _N G_a as a scheme
ideas.modern_name: N-torsion of G_a (a non-flat group scheme over Z)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up a projective system of ring schemes O_N (scheme-theoretic 'congruence' rings over Spec Z) and their unit group schemes. He explicitly leaves open their structure and their projective limit, a group-scheme-level model of Ẑ and Ẑ^*.
missed.quote: Je ne vais pas regarder de plus près la structure de ces systèmes projectifs, ni examiner les limites projectives
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A pro-ring-scheme over Z whose unit groups mix G_m- and G_a-type fibres could be a model for 'arithmetic' versions of Ẑ^*. That would bear on the Grothendieck–Teichmüller / Galois action context of the Longue Marche. The idea is only sketched here.

missed.claim: The unit group (1+NZ)^* is precisely the Sekiguchi–Oort–Suwa / Waterhouse–Weisfeiler deformation group scheme G^{(N)}. Grothendieck arrives at it naturally, in the 1980s, as a congruence subgroup scheme in his Galois–Teichmüller setting with N = 12.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an independent appearance of the G_m–G_a interpolation tied to level-N structures and to the number 12 of SL_2(Z). It is of historical interest, but the object itself is well known.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly routine scheme-theoretic bookkeeping of a congruence unit group. The rediscovery of the G^{(λ)} group scheme and the unexplored pro-system of ring schemes are mildly interesting, but the page is sketchy and explicitly stops short of developing them.
transcription_corrections: The ring-scheme symbol rendered as 'Z̃' (hat-Z) is a hand-drawn double-struck letter; it most likely denotes the additive ring scheme (G_a-like) over S_0, not the profinite completion.
'𝔻_N' / '𝕆_N' are the same circled/double-struck O_N as on neighbouring pages; read O_N consistently.
(76) reads roughly 'O_N^* → O_1^* = O^* = G_m', i.e. the last term may be G_m rather than 'Z̃^*_[?]'.
Line before (77): 'Ces noyaux sont formés des éléments du syst. des'.
Final words: 'isomorphe à _N Z̃_0', i.e. the N-torsion subscheme.
